summary: Danmarks Statistik publishes convictions every year by herkomst (Danish origin; immigrants and descendants from Western and non-Western countries) and by country of origin, including sexual offences against children, and the Justice Ministry's homicide study links victim and perpetrator herkomst. Herkomst is a birth-country and citizenship proxy, not ethnicity, and no child victims are published by herkomst outside homicide.

nations.National (Danmarks Statistik, Justice Mi: Conviction statistics by herkomst and country of origin; homicide and crime-and-herkomst studies; Center mod Menneskehandel trafficking statistics.

european_title: Not recorded by any Danish source
european_note: Danish statistics record herkomst, built from the birth country and citizenship of the person and their parents, never ethnicity. 'Danish origin' is the closest group to ethnic Europeans but is a proxy: it includes grandchildren of immigrants (40,286 children of descendants were classed as Danish origin on 1 January 2026, most with Turkish, Pakistani or Lebanese roots) and anyone with one Danish-born Danish-citizen parent. 'Western' is not 'European' (it includes the USA, Canada, Australia and New Zealand), and 'non-Western' includes non-EU Europe such as Ukraine, Russia and the Balkans.

harms.label: Sexual offences against children (convictions)
harms.intro: Danmarks Statistik counts 81 persons found guilty of sexual offences against a child under 15 and 36 against a child under 12 in 2025 (350 and 180 over 2021-2025). Both are published every year by herkomst and by country of origin. No victims are published by herkomst.

victims.text: Danmarks Statistik publishes victims of reported crime by age and sex only (STRAF5, LIGEPB1); no herkomst.

perpetrators.scope: Denmark, persons found guilty of a sexual offence against a child under 15, 2021-2025 combined
perpetrators.rate_reason: Danmarks Statistik does not publish rates for these offences by herkomst; not calculated here.
perpetrators.share_note: Shares calculated here from StatBank STRFNA10 counts (Danish origin 306, Western immigrants 8, non-Western immigrants 20, Western descendants 2, non-Western descendants 14). Persons resident in Denmark found guilty (convictions, fines and similar decisions), counted once by main offence per year. Herkomst (Danmarks Statistik): 'Danish origin' means at least one parent who is both a Danish citizen and born in Denmark, wherever the person was born, so it includes grandchildren of immigrants and children with one immigrant parent. Immigrants are born abroad and descendants born in Denmark with no such parent. 'Western' means the EU, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the UK, the Vatican, Canada, the USA, Australia and New Zealand; 'non-Western' is every other country, including non-EU Europe (Ukraine, Russia, Serbia, Bosnia, Turkey). This is a birth-country and citizenship proxy, not ethnicity.

cross.text: Convictions are not published with the herkomst of the victim, so no table links victim and perpetrator.

harms.label: Homicide (Justice Ministry study and convictions)
harms.intro: The Justice Ministry's study 'Drab i Danmark 2017-2021' covers all 223 homicides: victims and perpetrators by herkomst, Western and non-Western splits, population shares and victim-perpetrator linkage. 19 victims (9%) were children; the report says 14 of the 19 were of Danish origin and just over half of their 10 perpetrators. StatBank also gives persons found guilty of homicide each year by herkomst (127 over 2021-2025, all victims).

harms.label: Trafficking in human beings (identified victims)
harms.intro: Center mod Menneskehandel (Social- og Boligstyrelsen) assessed 101 people as trafficked in 2025: 78 women and 23 men, 55 for sexual exploitation, one minor (a 15-year-old girl). They came from 31 countries, most often Thailand (24), Ukraine (11), Vietnam (9), Romania (8) and Nigeria (8); none was Danish. No trafficker nationality is published, and trafficking convictions are not separated in StatBank's herkomst tables.

breakdown.why: Danmarks Statistik gives persons found guilty of sexual offences against children under 12 and under 15 every year by herkomst (Danish origin, Western and non-Western immigrants and descendants; 36 and 81 in 2025) and by 75 countries of origin. Residents only, convictions not victims; no child victims by herkomst. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Persons guilty of violence (5,953 in 2025) by herkomst and country of origin, all victims; the Justice Ministry publishes age-standardised indices by herkomst. No child victims of violence by herkomst (victim tables give age and sex only). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The Justice Ministry's 'Drab i Danmark 2017-2021' gives the 223 victims and 248 perpetrators by herkomst with Western/non-Western splits, population shares and victim-perpetrator linkage (83% same group for Danish-origin victims); child homicides (19) are described only in a sentence. Persons guilty of homicide are published annually by herkomst and country of origin. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Center mod Menneskehandel lists the 101 people identified as trafficked in 2025 by nationality (31 countries, no Danes; 1 minor; 55 sexual exploitation). No trafficker nationality. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Only grooming convictions by herkomst (3 in 2025, all Danish origin); child sexual abuse material is not separated in the herkomst tables. No victims by herkomst. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Denmark scores 14% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. Danmarks Statistik publishes convictions every year by herkomst (Danish origin, immigrants and descendants from Western and non-Western countries) and by country of origin, including for sexual offences against children, and the Justice Ministry's homicide study links victim and perpetrator herkomst. But herkomst is built from parents' birth country and citizenship, a proxy, there are no child victims by herkomst outside homicide, and grandchildren of immigrants count as Danish origin.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No paired child table. The homicide study publishes two linkage percentages for all ages, not a child cross-table.
